Interesting ketiv/qere cases in NAEE

Features of interest · NAEE book links · Dataset documentation

In NAEE (the Near-Aleppo example edition), the pointed ketiv is the primary text, with the pointed qere above it and a curved box or "cartouche" around the ketiv/qere pair. When the qere is wider, the ketiv is centered beneath it.

  1. 2 Samuel 8:3 — a wide qere
  2. Isaiah 54:16 — a final dalet carrier
  3. Genesis 30:11 — two qere atoms
  4. Qere without ketiv
  5. Isaiah 26:20 — MAM ketiv/qere inside a three-atom maqaf compound
  6. 1 Chronicles 9:4 — a two-atom qere inside a maqaf compound

2 Samuel 8:3 — a wide qere

The qere is a maqaf compound above a shorter ketiv atom.

וַיַּ֣ךְ דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר בֶּן־רְחֹ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ צוֹבָ֑ה בְּלֶכְתּ֕וֹ לְהָשִׁ֥יב יָד֖וֹ בִּֽנְהַר(בִּֽנְהַר־פְּרָֽת)׃

Isaiah 54:16 — a final dalet carrier

The single-atom qere has an additional he. The ketiv's final-nun dagesh, tsere and mahapakh are displayed on an artificial dalet carrier immediately after the nun, without a space. Carrier notation usually indicates that marks are orphaned or that the letter they belong to is unclear. In this case, a strong argument can be made that the marks belong to the final nun. We use carrier (orphan) syntax mainly because many fonts have difficulty displaying these marks on a final nun.

הִן«דֵּ֤»(הִנֵּ֤ה) אָנֹכִי֙ בָּרָ֣אתִי חָרָ֔שׁ נֹפֵחַ֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ פֶּחָ֔ם וּמוֹצִ֥יא כְלִ֖י לְמַעֲשֵׂ֑הוּ וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּרָ֥אתִי מַשְׁחִ֖ית לְחַבֵּֽל׃

Genesis 30:11 — two qere atoms

The qere has two space-separated atoms above one ketiv atom.

וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לֵאָ֖ה בָּ֣גָ֑ד(בָּ֣א גָ֑ד) וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ גָּֽד׃

Qere without ketiv

Ruth 3:5 and Judges 20:13 show qere without ketiv; in Ruth 3:5 there is no niqqud for the ketiv whereas in Judges 20:13 there is.

Qere without ketiv: manuscript readings and crops

Ruth 3:5

וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֶ֑יהָ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמְרִ֥י «»(אֵלַ֖י) אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃

Judges 20:13

וְעַתָּ֡ה תְּנוּ֩ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים בְּנֵי־בְלִיַּ֜עַל אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּגִּבְעָה֙ וּנְמִיתֵ֔ם וּנְבַעֲרָ֥ה רָעָ֖ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א אָבוּ֙ «אְאֵ֣»(בְּנֵ֣י) בִנְיָמִ֔ן לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ בְּק֖וֹל אֲחֵיהֶ֥ם בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

Isaiah 26:20 — MAM ketiv/qere inside a three-atom maqaf compound

In MAM, the ketiv יעבור and qere יַעֲבׇר occupy the middle atom of a compound starting with עַד־ and ending with זָֽעַם. NAEE displays עַד־יַעֲבָור־זָֽעַם, with no qere above the middle atom. This follows MAM's note, which reports the ketiv and no qere note in the Aleppo Codex. In forming the near-Aleppo dataset, we inferred the ketiv's pointing from the qere.

Compare this verse in MAM-with-doc

… חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־רֶ֖גַע עַד־יַעֲבָור־זָֽעַם׃

1 Chronicles 9:4 — a two-atom qere inside a maqaf compound

The single ketiv atom בנימן has a two-atom qere.

When viewed in context, the ketiv forms a four-atom maqaf compound:

בֶן־בָּנִ֔ימִן־בְּנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ

In contrast, the qere forms a two-atom maqaf compound followed by a three-atom maqaf compound:

בֶן־בָּנִ֔י מִן־בְּנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ

עוּתַ֨י בֶּן־עַמִּיה֤וּד בֶּן־עָמְרִי֙ בֶּן־אִמְרִ֣י בֶן־בָּנִ֔ימִן־(בָּנִ֔י מִן־)בְּנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ בֶּן־יְהוּדָֽה׃
